newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Hundreds flee Grozny amid rumours of assault.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds flee Grozny amid rumours of assault.

text.p: Hundreds of civilians left their homes in the Chechen capital Grozny on Saturday, continuing an exodus sparked by persistent rumours of an assault on the city by forces loyal to the pro-Moscow local government.
Officials at two police command posts in the city, jointly staffed by separatist fighters and Russian troops following a peace deal late last month, said the new rumours were unfounded.

Doku Zavgayev, the loyalist pro-Russian leader forced out of Grozny six weeks ago by the separatist guerrillas, denied the rumours on Friday, insisting his supporters, concentrated in the north of the mainly Moslem region, were not ready to fight.
But many local residents, forced to flee in their tens of thousands by last month's battle, were taking no chances.
The date of the assault on August 6 by pro-independence forces from the south was widely rumoured in advance. The latest talk was that the loyalists would strike on Sunday.
"It's just a panic put about by Zavgayev's people," the Chechen commander at one joint command post told Reuters.
Zavgayev's spokesman said last week the loyalists had 4,000 men under arms -- a figure close to that for the separatists.

But many local people are sceptical about the pro-Moscow faction's strength. Significant numbers of police and other Chechen forces supposedly loyal to Zavgayev either refused to fight or went over to the rebels during the battle last month.

Zavgayev, once the Soviet-era regional leader who was elected last December in a vote riddled with irregularities, complained bitterly about being left out of a peace deal reached by Kremlin envoy Alexander Lebed and the separatist commander.
He said last week, however, he was prepared to try to arrange a provisional coalition government with the rebels.

The co-chairman of a separatist-dominated popular assembly, boycotted by Zavgayev last week, told Interfax news agency on Saturday that the group intended to present a proposed list of ministers to the separatist leadership later in the day.
Three ministers in Zavgayev's cabinet were reported to be ready to join the coalition, but Zavgayev has kept his distance.
